rule: One reader, one pass, no model. For each case the reader had the whole Deviations entry, the ticket's acceptance criteria, the follow-up issue with its last comments, and the review verdicts on the pull request. A case is named <repo>#<pull request>/<entry number>. `filed` is 36 of the 274 entries that filed a new issue, at even steps in merge order (about every 8th). `stated` is every n-th 'Known defect left unfixed' entry that filed nothing, in the four-field form, on a pull request that closed its ticket. `narrowed` is the same draw over 'Scope narrowing' entries; it was read after the tables had shown how large that pile is, and it splits `a` three ways. `known` is the one case that started the question, read the same way and counted in neither sample.

part.a: Part of an acceptance criterion's own words was left undone, or done another way.
part.a-left: A criterion's own words, and work is left over: something the criterion asked for is still not there after the merge.
part.a-way: A criterion's own words, done another way. The builder says the point of the criterion is met, and nothing is left over.
part.a-proof: A criterion's own words about proof: a run or a hand check it asked for was done a weaker way, or left to the hosted checks.
part.ticket: Asked for in the ticket's text or a ruling on it, but in no criterion.
part.told: The ticket itself said: leave this. In the filed sample it also said: file it.
part.b-own: Next to the ticket: a limit or a loose end of the work this pull request added, that no criterion names.
part.b-near: Next to the ticket: an older or neighbouring problem the builder noticed on the way.
part.tool: Not a gap in the product: a check that was red or could not run for a reason outside the change.
part.not: Not a gap at all: a choice the builder made and disclosed under this label.

why.scope: Outside this ticket: older than the change, another ticket's ground, or somebody else's code.
why.blocked: Could not be done from here: another defect, a missing tool, a missing input or a rule stood in the way.
why.decision: Needs a person's ruling or a design choice the builder should not make alone.
why.bigger: Bigger than the ticket: its own build.
why.wrong: The criterion could not be met as written: it was out of date, it contradicted itself, or it named a thing that does not exist.

review.pass_noted: PASS. The verdict names the leftover and accepts it.
review.pass_limit: PASS, with the criterion itself marked as partly met: 'PARTIAL', 'DEFERRED', 'OPEN for 4', 'substance met', 'with a named limit'.
review.advisory: The pull request touched the pipeline's own rules, so the reviewer's word was advice and a person approved the merge.
review.pass_plain: PASS, and the verdict does not mention the leftover.

failed.no: No verdict failed the pull request over this leftover.
failed.yes: A verdict first failed the pull request over this leftover, and a later round passed with the leftover still there.

asked.no: Nobody asked the owner about the leftover.
asked.approval: The owner had to approve the merge anyway, because the pull request touched the pipeline's own rules. Nothing shows the leftover was the question.
asked.before: The owner was asked about this leftover, or ruled on it, before the merge.
asked.after: The follow-up issue itself became the question to the owner, after the merge.

tracked.no: Nothing tracks it. The entry is the only record.
tracked.nothing: Nothing is left to track: the point of the criterion was met another way, or the missing proof arrived before the merge.
tracked.reviewer: Left to the reviewer or to triage to decide. Nothing was filed.
tracked.ticket: The entry names a ticket that already covers it, in words the matcher did not catch.
tracked.said: The entry says it was filed, and gives no number.
tracked.record: Written into a decision record or a doc comment, not a ticket.
